overall_summary: Bitcoin momentum remains strong with heavy ETF inflows, a major short squeeze, and fresh debasement tailwinds from Treasury buybacks. Institutional voices and ETH relative strength add to the constructive tone. Geopolitical and tariff risks are real but are taking a back seat to the crypto-specific bid for now.
key_points: BTC holds $78K after strongest week in years
Spot Bitcoin ETFs see $1.92B weekly inflows
Treasury buybacks fuel debasement trade narrative
Tariffs and Iran tensions add macro caution

items.title: Bitcoin Posts Second-Best Week Since 2021, Holds Above $78K
items.summary: Bitcoin just wrapped one of its strongest weeks in years, up roughly 22 to 24 percent, climbing from the low 60 thousands to test near 80 thousand before settling and then pushing fresh daily highs above 78 thousand on Monday alongside gold. The move broke bitcoin and ether above their 200-day moving averages after months of tight consolidation. Traders should care because this is confirmed momentum with macro tailwinds still in play, though all eyes now turn to the Jackson Hole symposium for the next catalyst or risk.
items.impact: Supports continued upside if key levels hold into Fed week

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Draw $1.92B in Strongest Week Since Late 2025
items.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs pulled in about 1.92 billion dollars net last week across all five sessions, their strongest haul since October 2025, while ether ETFs added nearly 700 million for a combined crypto ETF total around 2.62 billion. Inflows tracked the price rally rather than leading it in some sessions, with big single days near 600 million. This is pure institutional demand that can absorb supply on dips and provide structural bid support if it stays sticky.
items.impact: Structural buying power underpins pullbacks and higher prices

items.title: Treasury Doubles Bond Buybacks, Ignites Debasement Trade and BTC Surge
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expanded long-dated bond buybacks to at least 4 billion dollars per operation, aiming to ease yields that hit multi-year highs. Yields barely budged lower, but the signal of official unease over debt costs and liquidity sparked a weaker dollar, gold rally, and bitcoin explosion as the debasement trade returned. Traders care because it reframes high yields as potentially bullish for scarce assets rather than a pure headwind, keeping the policy put narrative alive.
items.impact: Macro liquidity signal favors hard assets like bitcoin over bonds

items.title: Over $4 Billion in Crypto Shorts Liquidated in Massive Squeeze
items.summary: The Treasury-triggered rally forced more than 4 billion dollars in bearish crypto positions to close, according to derivatives trackers, with shorts dominating liquidations by a wide margin and cascading buying pressure. Bitcoin blasted through the prior 62 to 67 thousand range that had trapped many shorts. This mechanical fuel amplified the move, but with shorts largely cleared and leveraged longs now building, the next leg depends on whether spot and ETF demand can carry the tape without more squeeze fuel.
items.impact: Cleared overhead supply but raises crowded-long unwind risk

items.title: Ray Dalio Urges Owning a Bit of Bitcoin Amid US Debt Risks
items.summary: Bridgewater founder Ray Dalio said investors should hold some bitcoin and 10 to 15 percent gold as protection against mounting US debt, deficits, and potential currency devaluation or financial repression. He tied recent Treasury stress and buybacks to the patterns in his debt-crisis framework, estimating a fuller crisis in about three years. High-profile endorsement like this reinforces the institutional and macro narrative that just drove the latest rally.
items.impact: Adds legitimacy and allocation interest from traditional finance

items.title: Ether Crushes Bitcoin as ETH/BTC Forms Bullish Golden Cross
items.summary: Ether outperformed bitcoin sharply last week with a 30-plus percent gain versus bitcoin's 23 percent, and the ETH/BTC ratio has printed a golden cross where the 50-day moving average crossed above the 200-day. Ether ETFs also saw strong inflows. This relative strength can signal broader altcoin rotation or risk-on extension if it holds, though past golden crosses on the pair have been mixed.
items.impact: Supports ETH leadership and potential altseason extension

items.title: Warsh Jackson Hole Debut Key for Rates Outlook
items.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole speech as chair this Friday amid the August 27-29 symposium focused on financial innovation. Markets are hungry for clues on sticky inflation and whether the Fed stays on hold or leans hawkish after the July hold at 3.5-3.75 percent. Traders should care because long-end yields have been volatile without clear guidance, and any signal could swing bond markets, the dollar, and risk assets including crypto.
items.impact: High volatility risk into Friday speech; unresolved policy path

items.title: Bessent Presser Today on Iran Sanctions and Buybacks
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent holds a press conference this afternoon expected to detail new Iran sanctions and elaborate on fiscal consolidation plus the upsized long-end Treasury buybacks. The buyback expansion to at least four billion dollars per operation starting September aims to ease pressure on longer yields after they spiked. Crypto traders should watch because successful jawboning of yields supports risk appetite while sanctions and oil geopolitics can drive safe-haven flows and dollar moves.
items.impact: Potential short-term yield relief or geo-risk spike

items.title: 10-Year Yield Eases to 4.71 Percent on Relief
items.summary: US 10-year Treasury yields pulled back about two basis points to around 4.71 percent as markets digested Bessent’s buyback and fiscal roadmap details. Longer bonds had pushed toward multi-year highs earlier amid debt supply and inflation worries, prompting the Treasury intervention. For traders this matters because lower long yields ease financial conditions and often lift Bitcoin and equities, though the level remains elevated and sensitive to data.
items.impact: Mild risk-on support if yields stabilize lower

items.title: PCE Inflation and GDP Revision Due Wednesday
items.summary: July core PCE, the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, and the second estimate of second-quarter GDP land Wednesday morning alongside personal income and spending. Core PCE is watched near 3.3 percent year-over-year with monthly expectations around 0.2 percent, while GDP advance was soft at roughly 1.5 percent. Crypto traders need this because hotter inflation could revive hike bets and pressure risk assets, while cooler prints or solid growth support the hold narrative into Jackson Hole.
items.impact: Major directional catalyst for rates and dollar mid-week

items.title: US Hits Canada with 50 Percent Tariffs on 20 Billion
items.summary: After talks collapsed late Friday the US imposed 50 percent tariffs on about 20 billion dollars of Canadian goods covering roughly five percent of exports, with Canada pledging dollar-for-dollar retaliation from September 8. The Canadian dollar came under pressure and North American trade friction is escalating. Traders should note this adds growth and inflation uncertainty that can weigh on risk sentiment and complicate the Fed’s path.
items.impact: Trade-war drag on growth expectations and risk appetite

items.title: Dollar Index Holds Near 99 After Weekly Losses
items.summary: The DXY is trading around 98.8 to 99 on Monday, showing modest firmness after last week’s declines driven by rising long yields, debt concerns, and the Treasury buyback announcement. Monthly performance remains soft as fiscal worries linger. A weaker or range-bound dollar has generally been supportive for Bitcoin, so traders should monitor whether yields or data break the recent pattern.
items.impact: Range-bound dollar keeps crypto conditions mixed-to-supportive

items.title: US Launches 'Economic D-Day' Sanctions Blitz on Iran
items.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is rolling out what he calls the single greatest financial offensive ever against Iran, aiming to sever every economic lifeline and isolate the regime plus any partners still dealing with it. Tehran calls the move desperate and has threatened to shut down all Gulf oil exports if the pressure continues. Traders should care because this hits the heart of global energy supply six months into the war, with secondary sanctions risk spooking China and others. Oil volatility and broader risk-off moves are the immediate market story.
items.impact: Heightened oil supply fears and risk-off pressure on equities and crypto

items.title: Iran Blacklists 45 Tankers, Threatens Seizure in Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's new Persian Gulf authority has blacklisted around 45 tankers including UAE and Saudi vessels for allegedly violating its transit rules in the Strait of Hormuz, warning of fines, detention or cargo confiscation. Any ships doing ship-to-ship transfers with them could also be hit. This escalates control over the chokepoint that normally handles a fifth of global oil. For traders it means fresh disruption risk to crude flows already running at a fraction of normal, keeping energy prices jumpy and risk assets on edge.
items.impact: Direct threat to oil transit raises energy prices and market volatility

items.title: US 50% Tariffs Hit Canada; Ottawa Vows Dollar-for-Dollar Retaliation
items.summary: After trade talks collapsed, the US imposed 50 percent tariffs on about 20 billion dollars of Canadian goods ranging from dairy and steel to hockey sticks. Prime Minister Mark Carney suspended negotiations and promised matching retaliatory tariffs starting September 8 on US steel, electronics, dairy and more. This is a fresh North American trade war between close allies. Crypto and risk traders should watch for growth hits, supply-chain pain and broader risk-off sentiment if it escalates.
items.impact: Trade friction weighs on North American growth and risk appetite

items.title: UK PM Burnham in Kyiv Offers Long-Range Missile Tech
items.summary: New British Prime Minister Andy Burnham made Kyiv his first foreign trip on Ukraine's Independence Day, pledging the UK is 100 percent behind the country and authorizing release of classified UK components data for Scalp long-range missiles so Ukraine can assemble them locally. He is also chairing a Coalition of the Willing meeting. Russia has already warned of consequences for British support. This signals continued Western escalation and longer war, keeping European security risk elevated for markets.
items.impact: Prolongs Ukraine conflict uncertainty without immediate new black-swan shock

items.title: Saudi Arabia Seeks State-Backed War Insurance for Ships
items.summary: Saudi Arabia is in talks with London brokers to set up a state-backed war-risk insurance scheme for ships and cargo as premiums soar and some insurers restrict or refuse cover due to the Iran conflict and Houthi attacks. The plan could provide up to around 186 million dollars cover per incident with a government backstop. This shows how the Middle East war is choking commercial shipping even for major producers. Energy traders note it as a sign of persistent elevated costs and logistics friction that supports higher oil prices.
items.impact: Signals ongoing shipping and insurance stress supporting oil risk premium

items.title: Pro-Tokayev Party Wins Landslide in Kazakhstan Election
items.summary: Kazakhstan's newly formed Adilet party, tied to President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, took over 71 percent of the vote in Sunday's parliamentary election for the new unicameral Kurultai. Turnout was about 74 percent and other parties clearing the threshold are also broadly supportive of the government. Tokayev has hinted he may seek another term. As a major energy and minerals exporter, political continuity matters for supply stability, though this result was widely expected and is not a market shock.
items.impact: Political continuity in key Central Asian resource exporter
